commits.summary: Add an allow list for false-positive findings: an agent proposes a finding by id, a person approves it at a terminal, and check stops raising that value without a rescan
commits.body: Work from session 0d3dce51, committed from another session at the user's request so that the repository could be pushed; its description here is read from the diff. Accepting a finding by id meant finding the value again with a scan of every file newer than the redaction stamp, and a class of false positives (version numbers that look like addresses) used to be settled by a new rule, which voided the stamp and rescanned everything. llm-dlc/allowlist.json settles them by value instead, through a new 'allow' command: listing entries with proposals masked, 'propose ID --reason' recording a proposal with the id, kind and masked value (open to agents), an approval step that prints the real values and asks a person once for 'false positive', direct entry of a value by a person, and 'drop' to remove entries. The list is published with its values, so it takes only the kinds the redactor leaves in a log and that are published anyway once accepted (public-ip, ipv6, mac-address, other-home-dir, auth-header, long-token); a finding the redactor would remove still goes through review accept, which keeps only a hash. The project settings deny agents the approval and direct-entry steps and direct edits to the list; CLAUDE.md, llm-dlc/README.md, the specification and the review-findings skill describe the new procedure, and the list of reviewed findings carries the entries a person recorded meanwhile. Verified: llm-dlc/tools/test_review.py, 25 tests, passes.
